alternate_names: Shri Lakshmi Narayan Mandir, Katra Manrai

history.summary: Built by Hindu migrants from Pakistan after Partition in Koharapeer, Katra Manrai (old Bareilly, near Budhwari Masjid), on land owned by Fazal-ul-Rahman, known as 'Chunne Miyan'. He first filed a suit against the construction, but after hearing the sermon of Shri HarMilapi Ji Maharaj of Haridwar he withdrew it and supported the temple financially - his name heads the donor list and the temple is named after him. Inaugurated on 16 May 1960 by President Dr. Rajendra Prasad. A celebrated symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity. No opening hours are published online (flagged); reviews recommend morning visits.

name: Chunne Miyan's Lakshmi Narayan Temple
town_description: Bareilly is a major city in western Uttar Pradesh on the northern Gangetic plain, traditionally called Nath Nagari for its cluster of ancient Shiva temples. A historic trade and cantonment town, it is known for zardozi embroidery, furniture and the Ala Hazrat dargah alongside its Hindu shrines, and is well connected by rail and road to Delhi and Lucknow.

travel.railway: Bareilly Junction (~2-3 km); in the old-city market area behind Bara Bazar
travel.road: Located in the congested Koharapeer market off Bara Bazar Road; autos and cycle-rickshaws easiest for the last stretch.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; mornings are best to avoid the market rush.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published online (verify locally); reviewers recommend morning visits.
